name: IEC clocked SR flip-flop
summary: IEC bistable with 1S and 1R inputs that act only under C1 control, giving a synchronous set-reset function.
description: Adding the C1 prefix to S and R makes them synchronous: they act only when C1 is active or on its active transition. The element therefore combines set-reset storage with clocking, which keeps state changes aligned with the rest of a synchronous system.

Clocked SR elements appear in function-block diagrams for PLCs and in state-machine documentation. On hardware schematics the same function is often implemented with a JK or D flip-flop and gating, so cross-reference the implementation.
The symbol needs a stated rule for 1S and 1R active together. Without S or R dependency or a note, that condition is undefined.
readingNotes: Prefix numbers on S and R show they are synchronous.
Look for a priority statement for both inputs active.
distinction: The unclocked IEC SR latch acts immediately on S and R.
